newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Azeris to sign three new oil deals with U.S firms.
newsitem.headline: Azeris to sign three new oil deals with U.S firms.

text.p: Azerbaijan's state oil company, SOCAR, plans to sign at least three new contracts with U.S. energy firms to develop Caspian Sea oil fields, a SOCAR official said on Monday.
Davud Babayev said the contracts, with Exxon Corp, Chevron Corp and Mobil Corp, would be signed when Azeri President Haydar Aliyev pays an official visit to the United States at the end of summer.
The three deals are the newest jewels in the bag for Azerbaijan, which has already signed five offshore contracts with foreign firms worth over $18 billion.

"We have received answers to our proposals with these three companies and they have accepted our conditions," Babayev said by telephone. "Now we are preparing these documents for signing during President Aliyev's visit to the United States.
"SOCAR plans on having not less than a 50 percent stake in each contract with the U.S. firms."
The deal with Exxon concerns the D-3 field in Azerbaijan's southern sector of the Caspian. The field may hold at least 100 million tonnes of crude.
Babayev said SOCAR would sign with Chevron on the Zeinalabdin Tagiev field, with possible recoverable reserves of 115 million tonnes of crude and 420 billion cubic meters of natural gas.

SOCAR and Mobil would sign on the D-30 and Oguz fields, 70-80 km southeast of the capital Baku, he said. SOCAR estimates Oguz may contain at least 40 million tonnes of crude and 20 billion cubic meters of natural gas. No figures were available for D-30.
Babayev cautioned that reserve estimates for the fields were preliminary.
Aliyev's official U.S. state visit, where he is scheduled to meet President Bill Clinton, will be the first ever by an Azeri leader.
Officials say it is an indication of the increasing commercial and political importance of the former Soviet republic, which sits on large energy reserves.
Babayev said other oil companies, including Shell Oil Co -- the U.S. unit of Royal Dutch/Shell Group -- Texaco Inc, Russia's LUKoil and Turkish Petroleum also might participate in the contracts.
Exxon and SOCAR already have a a memorandum of understanding for offshore oilfields D-3, D-9 and D-38.
Azerbaijan has signed a series of major contracts with foreign firms to develop its massive offshore reserves.
The largest to date, worth $8 billion, is with a consortium of firms led by a British Petroleum / Den norske stats oljeselskap (Statoil) alliance.
